sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Phelps County?
sections.html:
Phelps County splits the job between two offices in the Rolla courthouse, 200 N Main Street, Rolla, MO 65401. The assessor sets the value. The collector bills and collects. Neither one sets the rate, which comes from the voters of each taxing district.

  • Assessor Tim Kean, Suite 126, (573) 458-6135, fax (573) 458-6149, open 8:00 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday
  • Collector Faith Barnes, Suite 129, (573) 458-6155, collectorgroup@phelpscounty.org, open 8:00 am to 4:30 pm weekdays through the lunch hour
  • County Clerk, (573) 458-6115, for questions about levies and tax rates
  • Recorder of Deeds Robin Kordes, (573) 458-6095, for the deed itself

The assessor's office tells callers it cannot discuss the dollar amount of a bill. It answers questions about assessed and market value only, and the collector answers the rest.

sections.h2: How is a Phelps County tax bill calculated?
sections.html:
The collector gives two formulas. Divide the assessed value by the adjustment factor to estimate the assessor's market value, and divide the assessed value by 100 and multiply by the levy to find the tax. Residential property is assessed at 19 percent of market value, agricultural at 12 percent and commercial at 32 percent, as RSMo 137.115 provides.

Take a Phelps County house at the Census median owner-occupied value of $206,500. At 19 percent, its assessed value is about $39,235. That number, in hundreds, is multiplied by the combined levy of the school, fire, city and other districts that cover the parcel. The collector notes you pay only the districts that apply to your address, not every levy in the county.

The assessor values real estate on a two year cycle, but the 2025 reassessment was bigger than usual. The assessor's site says the state tax commission found local values slipped out of the 90 to 110 percent compliance band after several years of rising sales prices. The average residential assessed value rose by about 10 percent that year, while agricultural and commercial values stayed flat except for new construction or changes in condition.

sections.h2: What if the Phelps County assessor visits my property?
sections.html:
Field staff are canvassing the whole county to refresh photos of homes and outbuildings and to note condition, with a focus on parcels not visited in more than five years. The assessor's site says the work is required by RSMo 137.130. Staff drive white Ford Bronco Sports with the assessor's logo on the doors and wear vests marked Phelps County Assessor, and each carries a county photo ID. Owners who asked to be called first are called when possible.

State law also limits large jumps. Under RSMo 137.115, a residential parcel cannot be raised by more than 15 percent without a physical inspection, unless new construction explains the increase, and the owner may ask for an interior look within thirty days of the notice.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Phelps County valuation?
sections.html:
Begin with a phone call or visit to the assessor at (573) 458-6135 and ask what comparable sales and condition notes support your number. Missouri law backs the owner who disagrees. When an assessor increases a value, the record owner must be told, and the increase can be reviewed by the county Board of Equalization, where the landowner is entitled to be heard (RSMo 137.180).

Ask the county clerk at (573) 458-6115 for the board's forms and filing deadline. Remember that the board decides appeals without presuming the assessor is right, and for increases of 15 percent or more outside new construction the assessor must prove the value (RSMo 138.060). After the board acts, the owner can appeal to the State Tax Commission within the statutory time or 30 days after the board's final action, whichever is later (RSMo 138.430).

sections.h2: When and how do I pay Phelps County real estate tax?
sections.html:
Bills go out in early November and must be paid by December 31. The collector says a payment not postmarked by that day incurs late fees. Mail should carry the stub, called the statement topper, because it holds the account number. The collector advises against bank bill pay services, which often send errors and no topper.

The collector keeps none of those fees. One check can cover any mix of real estate and personal property statements, but the amount must be exact because the office cannot process a payment written for the wrong sum. Installment plans exist for real estate and personal property, so ask at the counter for the form. If you have not received a bill by Thanksgiving, call right away.

sections.h2: Is there a senior tax freeze in Phelps County?
sections.html:
Yes. Phelps County seniors may qualify for a freeze on real estate taxes under Senate Bill 190 as expanded by Senate Bill 756. The applicant must be at least 62 by December 31 of the application year, own and live in the home as a primary residence, and be responsible for its taxes. Only one owner needs to be 62.

The application period for base year 2026 ran from March 1 through May 31, 2026, and it has closed. The freeze starts with the 2027 tax year, and the collector asks for at least 90 days to process. After that, participants send an affidavit every year during the same March through May window.

  • The freeze covers one primary residence only and is not retroactive to age 62.
  • It does not carry over to a new home; a move means a new application and a new base year.
  • A transfer of title removes the home from the program, as does a missed annual affidavit.
  • Debt levies and newly voted tax increases still show on the bill.

Questions go to the collector at (573) 458-6155 or seniortaxrelief@phelpscounty.org.

sections.h2: What happens when Phelps County property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels are auctioned once a year on the fourth Monday in August, starting at 10:00 am in the Community Room of the Phelps County Courthouse. The collector cites RSMo 140.150 for the date. The 2026 sale has passed, and the next one falls in August 2027. Notice runs in the Rolla Daily News on three consecutive Wednesdays beforehand, and the list appears on the collector's website.

A buyer does not own the house right away. The owner, a lienholder or an occupant can redeem during the year after the sale by paying the collector the purchase amount and costs, and the buyer earns simple interest of 10 percent a year on the tax and cost portion. Phelps County has advertised many more parcels than it sells, since most owners pay before the day arrives. A seller who is behind should pay up or sell before the notice is published.

sections.h2: What is Phelps County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Phelps County lies in the Missouri Ozarks, was organized on November 13, 1857 and named for John S. Phelps. Rolla is both the seat and the largest city, home to Missouri University of Science and Technology. The county also includes St. James, Newburg, Doolittle and Edgar Springs, and it is crossed by I-44, US 63 and Routes 8, 68 and 72. Part of the Mark Twain National Forest lies inside its borders. School districts include Rolla 31, St. James R-I, Newburg R-II and Phelps County R-III.

faqs.q: What is the Phelps County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: December 31. Bills are mailed in early November, and a payment not postmarked by December 31 incurs late fees.

faqs.q: Does the Phelps County assessor set my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The assessor sets value only. Each taxing district sets its levy by a vote of its residents, and the county clerk at (573) 458-6115 can answer rate questions.

faqs.q: Who gets the tax bill if I bought my Phelps County house mid-year?
faqs.a: The new owner pays the bill when it comes due. The collector says the buyer receives a credit at closing for the tax the seller owed for the year, and bills show the previous owner's name if the sale came after September 1.

faqs.q: Can I still apply for the Phelps County senior tax freeze this year?
faqs.a: No. The 2026 application window closed May 31, 2026. Call the collector at (573) 458-6155 to learn when applications reopen.

faqs.q: When is the Phelps County tax sale?
faqs.a: On the fourth Monday in August at 10:00 am, in the courthouse Community Room in Rolla. This year's date has passed.
